title: stakeholder-sandbox-canary-playbook-daily-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, daily-facing sandbox for cross-functional stewards running small canaries and A/B exposures that involve stakeholders across Product, SRE, Observability, and Solutions. The goal is: make low-friction, repeatable decisions for 0.1%-5% exposures while keeping clear human gates and fast reversion paths.

Audience:
- Activation steward (primary): runs daily checks and triages
- Product PM: owns hypothesis and acceptance criteria
- Observability lead: validates signals and thresholds
- SRE/Infra: provides rollback and capacity support
- Solutions/SE: customer-facing briefing if needed

Context / When to use this doc:
- Microcanary spins for an LLM prompt change, reranker tweak, or model-variant routing experiment
- Small A/B experiments that could materially affect latency/cost or surface-level safety signals
- Situations where stakeholders need an easily reproducible playbook and comms templates

Quick-start (1-hour steward checklist):
1) Confirm hypothesis and acceptance metrics with PM (Slack: #product-rollouts).
2) Validate telemetry: load the two queries in Observability (see "Observability queries" below).
3) Allocate traffic slice: pick microcohort size (0.5% default).
4) Start canary through Orchestrator UI or CLI (note time, commit id, model variant).
5) Watch first 10 minutes for P95 and error spike; fill live play-by-play in the daybook.
6) If no red signals after 60 minutes, escalate to stakeholders for curated 3-hour watch.
7) On any red signal, follow rollback script and notify via Slack + Pager if needed.

Three-tier sentinel design (how we reason about signals):
- Tier 1: Safety/critical (immediate rollback) — hallucination tokens > baseline, content-moderation flag rate increase > 3x, crashes or 5xxs.
- Tier 2: Operational (fast mitigation) — P95 latency > +200ms above baseline sustained for 5 mins, error rate > 0.5% absolute increase, token-cost per request increase > 20% over baseline.
- Tier 3: Behavioral drift (slow watch) — user-facing quality metrics (CTR, acceptance) shifting, subtle toxicity trends, long tail latency jitter.

Examples of concrete thresholds (starting recommendations):
- P95 latency: baseline = 420ms. Alert if > 650ms for 5 consecutive min.
- Token cost: baseline average 12 tokens/response; gate if mean tokens > 15 for 1000 requests.
- Safety flags: moderation-tagged responses > 0.6% => immediate pause.
- Error rate: baseline 0.12% -> gate if > 0.6% (absolute increase +0.48%).

Traffic allocation and cohort design notes:
- Default microcohort: 0.5% of global traffic, random sampling with weighting by geography and customer tier.
- For user-affecting features (UI textual changes), bias toward internal beta users and 10% of pro-tier to limit blast radius.
- Use stratified sampling where possible (device, locale, request size). Avoid sampling only on headers that correlate with heavy tail sequences.

Runbook snippets (CLI/Orchestrator):
- Start a canary (example):
  rwinf rollout start --env=prod --model=redwood-v2-slim --slice=0.5% --meta="prompt-tuning-v3"
- Immediate rollback (example):
  rwinf rollout set --id=canary-20260216-42 --percent=0 --reason="auto-rollback: safety-flag spike"
- Partial reversion (move 0.5% -> 0.1% of traffic):
  rwinf rollout set --id=canary-20260216-42 --percent=0.1 --note="gradual-backdown for latency investigation"

Comms templates (Slack):
- Starting notice (channel #product-rollouts):
  "Heads-up: starting microcanary 0.5% for prompt-tuning-v3 against prod on model redwood-v2-slim. Steward: @samira. Watchlist: P95 latency, moderation flags, token cost. Will report at +60m unless earlier action required."
- Rollback notice:
  "ACTION: Pausing microcanary redwood-v2-slim prompt-tuning-v3 at 0.5% due to moderation flags (0.85%). Reverted to baseline. Oncall: @tom-nguyen investigating. Tickets: JIRA-OPS-987."
- Postmortem starter: link to postmortem template + brief timeline + logs snapshot.

Escalation and phone-tree (when to page):
- Page SRE (pager) if any Tier 1 event (sustained safety spike or crash).
- If Tier 2 persists > 30 minutes after mitigation, page oncall for investigation.
- Stakeholder rotation: steward -> product PM -> obs lead -> SRE lead. If external customer impact suspected, CC solutions@redwood.com and prepare a short customer brief (template included).

Observability queries (copy into console):
- Latency P95 (PromQL-ish):
  percentile_over_time(0.95, request_latency_ms{model="redwood-v2-slim",route!="health"}[5m])
- Safety flag rate:
  sum(rate(moderation_flag_total{variant!~"baseline"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
- Token cost trend (moving avg):
  avg_over_time(tokens_consumed_per_request{model="redwood-v2-slim"}[15m])
- Error counts:
  increase(http_server_errors_total{route!="health"}[5m])

Daybook / logging discipline (what steward must record live):
- timestamp | action | slice% | signal observed | immediate action | follow-up owner
- Example: 2026-02-16T14:03Z | start canary | 0.5% | P95=710ms | drop to 0.1% | @obs-lead to review kernel scheduling

Simulation checklist (before a critical 2%-5% exposure):
- Run synthetic traffic with long-tail sequences (> 4k tokens) to validate memory usage.
- Spike test: 3x MPOPS for 2 minutes to validate autoscaler cadence.
- Failure injection: drop model variant for 60s and validate graceful fallback to lower-tier model.

Cost gating guidance:
- If per-minute token spend crosses 2x baseline absolute for a sustained 10-minute window OR overall projected monthly delta > 12% (based on commit), automatically pause and notify finance-signal.
- Add a cost-sentinel dashboard to the canary run card; steward must check at +15m and +60m.

Stakeholder-facing briefing template (one paragraph):
- What changed, why, scope (percent + cohorts), primary success metrics, monitoring plan, rollback path, anticipated dates for follow-up + decision. Keep it < 6 sentences.

Postmortem/Retro starter (if rollback):
- Timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigating actions, follow-up tickets (owner + due date), customer impact statement, lessons learned. Use the lightweight template linked in linked_artifacts below.

Open questions / unresolved items (working):
- Should microcohorts default to weighted sampling by request size? (affects P95 comparability) — ACTION: @priya to draft recommendation (JIRA: ENG-1123).
- Can we gate on model KV cache hit ratio as an early indicator for token inflation? Observability currently lacks a direct metric. — ACTION: @ravi to add instrumentation ticket (#github: repo/telemetry PR).
- Need an automated canary-fallback path for regional capacity shortages (multi-region routing). Who owns orchestration policy changes?

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize Tier thresholds in alerting (obs lead) — due 2026-03-05.
- Instrument KV cache hit ratio in telemetry (ravi) — draft PR due 2026-03-10.
- Run a rehearsal tabletop with 3 stewards next week and capture handoff timings.

Linked artifacts / references:
- Confluence: canary-runbook-template (id: CONF-6418)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-987 (recent incident), ENG-1123 (sampling proposal)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-orchestrator/pull/412

Daybook sample (live):
- 2026-02-28T09:00Z | start canary | 0.5% | baseline | monitoring | @samira
- 2026-02-28T09:12Z | observe | 0.5% | token cost +22% | reduce to 0.2% | @samira
- 2026-02-28T09:18Z | observe | 0.2% | moderation flag 0.82% (Tier1) | rollback to 0% and notify | Page SRE

Notes to self / steward tips (informal):
- Keep the first 20 minutes conservative: the system often has short-lived tail behavior when caches warm.
- If collaborating with Solutions for a customer pilot, pre-author a shorter rollback statement to speed comms.
- Favor human-gated pauses over automated hard-kill when the signal is borderline — we can always escalate to full revert.

Owner: Samira Patel (steward).
